title: AP Precalculus 2.2 — Changes in Linear and Exponential Functions Practice
question: Ten practice questions: tables, point forms, two points and sequences as linear or exponential functions.
intro:
**Quick recap:**

- Linear (constant difference):

\[
f(x)=b+mx
\]

- Linear through \((x_i,\ y_i)\):

\[
f(x)=y_i+m(x-x_i)
\]

- Exponential (constant ratio):

\[
f(x)=a\,b^{x}
\]

- Exponential through \((x_i,\ y_i)\):

\[
f(x)=y_i\,b^{(x-x_i)}
\]

- Arithmetic \(a_n=a_0+dn\) becomes linear. Geometric \(g_n=g_0r^n\) becomes exponential.

**A calculator is allowed. Show your calculation before choosing A–D.**

questions.title: Table · Constant difference
questions.prompt:
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3\\
\hline
y & 7 & 11 & 15 & 19
\end{array}
\]

Which function matches the table?
questions.solution_title: Equal steps in x add the same amount
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
11-7 &= 4 \\
15-11 &= 4 \\
19-15 &= 4
\end{aligned}
\]

The difference is constant, so the function is linear with \(b=7\) and \(m=4\):

\[
\boxed{f(x)=7+4x}
\]

- Not \(7\cdot4^x\): that multiplies by \(4\) each step, giving \(7,\ 28,\ 112\).
- Not \(4+7x\): the start value is \(f(0)=7\), so \(7\) is \(b\), not the slope.

questions.title: Table · Constant ratio
questions.prompt:
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3\\
\hline
y & 2 & 6 & 18 & 54
\end{array}
\]

Which function matches the table?
questions.solution_title: Equal steps in x multiply by the same number
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{6}{2} &= 3 \\
\frac{18}{6} &= 3 \\
\frac{54}{18} &= 3
\end{aligned}
\]

The ratio is constant, so the function is exponential with \(a=2\) and \(b=3\):

\[
\boxed{f(x)=2\cdot3^{x}}
\]

- Not \(2+4x\): it fits the first two points only (\(2,\ 6\)), then gives \(10\), not \(18\).
- Not \(3\cdot2^x\): the start value \(f(0)\) is \(2\), and the ratio is \(3\).

questions.title: Table · Halving each step
questions.prompt:
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3\\
\hline
y & 80 & 40 & 20 & 10
\end{array}
\]

Which function matches the table?
questions.solution_title: Each output is half of the one before
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{40}{80} &= 0.5 \\
\frac{20}{40} &= 0.5 \\
\frac{10}{20} &= 0.5
\end{aligned}
\]

The ratio is constant, so

\[
\boxed{f(x)=80(0.5)^{x}}
\]

- Not \(80-40x\): it fits \(80,\ 40\), then gives \(0\) instead of \(20\). Check every point, not two.
- Not \(80\cdot2^x\): the outputs get smaller, so the ratio is below \(1\).

questions.title: Linear · Slope and a point
questions.prompt:
A linear function has slope \(4\) and passes through the point \((2,\ 11)\).

Find \(f(5)\).
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(x) &= y_i+m(x-x_i) \\
f(x) &= 11+4(x-2)
\end{aligned}
\]

Put in \(x=5\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
f(5) &= 11+4(5-2) \\
&= 11+12 \\
&= \boxed{23}
\end{aligned}
\]

- From \(x=2\) to \(x=5\) is \(3\) steps, and each step adds \(4\).
- Not \(31\): \(11+4\cdot5\) forgets to subtract \(x_i=2\).
- Not \(15\): that adds only one step of \(4\).

questions.title: Exponential · Ratio and a point
questions.prompt:
An exponential function passes through \((1,\ 6)\).

Its outputs triple for every increase of \(1\) in \(x\).

Find \(f(3)\).
questions.solution_title: Use the point form with ratio 3

questions.title: Sequence → function · Arithmetic
questions.prompt:
An arithmetic sequence is

\[
a_n=5+2n
\]

Which function extends it to all real inputs \(x\)?
questions.solution_title: Match the parts: a₀ → b, d → m, n → x
questions.solution:
Arithmetic matches linear:

\[
\begin{aligned}
a_n &= a_0+dn \\
f(x) &= b+mx
\end{aligned}
\]

With \(a_0=5\) and \(d=2\):

\[
\boxed{f(x)=5+2x}
\]

- Not \(5\cdot2^x\): that is geometric (multiply by \(2\)). This sequence **adds** \(2\).
- Not \(2+5x\): the start value \(5\) and the step \(2\) are swapped.

questions.title: Sequence → function · Allowed inputs
questions.prompt:
A geometric sequence is

\[
g_n=3\cdot2^{n}
\]

The matching exponential function is

\[
f(x)=3\cdot2^{x}
\]

Which input can \(f\) use, but the sequence cannot?
questions.solution_title: A sequence uses whole numbers only
questions.solution:
- The sequence has a 0th, 1st, 2nd … term: \(n\) is a whole number.
- The function accepts every real \(x\).

So the input is

\[
\boxed{2.5}
\]

\[
\begin{aligned}
f(2.5) &= 3\cdot2^{2.5} \\
&\approx 16.97
\end{aligned}
\]

- Not \(0\), \(1\) or \(4\): both the sequence and the function can use these.

questions.title: Linear · Two points
questions.prompt:
A linear function has

\[
f(1)=5
\]

and

\[
f(4)=17
\]

Find \(f(0)\).
questions.solution_title: Slope first, then step back to x = 0

questions.title: Exponential · Two points
questions.prompt:
An exponential function has

\[
g(0)=3
\]

and

\[
g(2)=27
\]

Its base is positive.

Find \(g(1)\).
questions.solution_title: Two steps multiply by b twice

questions.title: Context · Which change is exponential?
questions.prompt: Which situation is modeled by an exponential function?
choices: A phone plan costs €20 more each year.
A town's population grows by \(5\%\) each year.
A candle gets \(3\) cm shorter each hour.
A taxi fare adds €1.20 for each km.
questions.solution_title: Equal steps multiply by the same factor
questions.solution:
- A \(5\%\) increase multiplies the population by the same factor each year:

\[
\begin{aligned}
b &= 1+0.05 \\
&= 1.05
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\boxed{\text{the population, } P(t)=P_0(1.05)^t}
\]

- The other three **add** (or take away) the same amount each step, so they are linear.

takeaway: Linear functions add the same amount over equal steps; exponential functions multiply by the same factor.
